--- title: "Pseudoword stress" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · L_ORAL_PROSODIA_ACENTO_PSEUDOP" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea L_ORAL_PROSODIA_ACENTO_PSEUDOP`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Acento de pseudopalabras*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/L_ORAL_PROSODIA_ACENTO_PSEUDOP.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Pseudoword stress, from age 4 to 5 (1,466 administrations in 2 cohorts). Stability across time points ρ = .33. AUC .55–.68 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2154 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | auditory stimuli | | Items | — | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | En esta actividad el alumno/a no puede ver la pantalla del ordenador y se le colocarán los auriculares a través de los cuales escuchará, uno por uno, 13 pares de secuencias. Las dos secuencias de cada par podrán ser iguales o diferentes (aunque muy similares) y la tarea es responder si son iguales o diferentes. *(Spanish)* | ## Theoretical framework The stress tasks measure **sensitivity to lexical stress**: perceiving which syllable sounds stronger. In Spanish, stress distinguishes words (*término*, *termino*, *terminó*), so it is part of the phonological representation of each word. In **word stress** (ages 6–7, 18 items), the child hears a three-syllable word and points to the stressed syllable. In **pseudoword stress** (ages 4–5), the child hears two almost identical sequences and decides whether they are the same or different. The hypothesis is that sensitivity to speech rhythm helps segment words and, through that route, learn to read. **What the evidence says:** - **In Spanish, suprasegmental sensitivity predicts reading beyond phonological awareness.** In 92 Grade 5 children, it explained unique variance in reading once phonological awareness and vocabulary were controlled [@calet2016suprasegmental]. - **In preschool, its effect goes through phonological awareness.** In 132 Spanish schoolchildren, preschoolers' lexical prosody influenced word and pseudoword reading only through phonological awareness [@roldan2026prosodic]. In 370 English-speaking Grade 1 children, the relation of stress with word reading was fully mediated by phonological and morphological awareness [@kim2016prosodic]. In 45 preschool children, lexical stress did not explain unique variance in reading once phonological awareness was controlled [@goodman2010stress]. Overall, the relation with reading is consistent, but its independent contribution is doubtful at the early ages, which are precisely those of these tasks. **What our data show.** - **Word stress.** α (2021) = .74, with hardly any ceiling effect (4%). Against persistent difficulty, AUC of .64–.66; against later low comprehension, only .53–.55, and against Woodcock-Muñoz, .52–.63. It is weakly related to reading and comprehension (ρ = .15–.26) and not at all to RAN. - **Pseudoword stress.** Stability ρ = .33 between two terms at age 4. Validity decreases with age: AUC of .68 at 4.1, .62 at 4.2 and .55 at age 5. It is related to phonological awareness (ρ ≈ .30) and not to RAN, as expected of a phonological skill. - **Caution.** The maximum score goes from 13 at 4.1 to 31 in the following sessions: these are probably different versions of the task and should not be compared without reviewing them. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.1| 2013| 181|2017/18 | 573| 565| 8| 24| | 4.2| 2013| 186|2017/18 | 566| 558| 8| 23| | 5.2| 2012| 187|2017/18 | 327| 324| 0| 16| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.1| 565| 2013| 7.40| 2.49| 7| -0.20| 1.24| 1.06| | 4.2| 558| 2013| 18.59| 6.73| 20| -0.78| 2.69| 0.36| | 5.2| 324| 2012| 21.60| 5.22| 22| -0.84| 0.31| 2.16| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 4.1| 565|0–12.4 |0–13 | | | 4.2| 558|0–29 |0–31 | | | 5.2| 324|9–30 |0–30 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .33 (median .33, 1 pairs of time points). Internal consistency from item-level responses is missing. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2013| 4.1| 4.2| 548| 0.30| 0.33| ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (4.1, r = .26); Phonological awareness (4.2, r = .33); Phonological awareness (5.2, r = .30). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .55–.68. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .58. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_PROSODIA_ACENTO_PSEUDOP_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .58–.61 (2 time points; 117–121 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.1| 565| 2013| 3| 5| 5| 6| 7| 9| 11| | 4.2| 558| 2013| 5| 10| 13| 15| 20| 24| 26| | 5.2| 324| 2012| 12| 15| 16| 18| 22| 25| 27| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_PROSODIA_ACENTO_PSEUDOP_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.1| 573| -0.011| 0.802| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.1| 570| 0.148| 0.076| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.1| 572| 0.015| 0.723| |School (ICC) | 4.1| 573| 0.117| | |School SES (ρ) | 4.2| 566| 0.096| 0.022| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.2| 563| 0.149| 0.079| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.2| 566| 0.079| 0.061| |School (ICC) | 4.2| 566| 0.185| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.2| 301| -0.104| 0.073| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.2| 325| 0.014| 0.896| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.2| 321| 0.215| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 5.2| 327| 0.250| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Pseudoword stress” (code 2154; LEEDUCA battery) assesses prosodic sensitivity (stress). Stimuli are presented auditorily and the child responds by selecting on the screen. The time limit is 90 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2012 and 2013 cohorts it was administered in 3 sessions, from 4 to 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 4 months) was ρ = .33. Stability across time points was ρ = .33. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .58. ## Pending issues - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
